An Act to amend the Defence of India Act, 1939.
1. Short title.---This Act
may be called the Defence of India (Amendment) Act, 1940.
Notes
Object.--"This Bill
seeks to make three minor amendments in the Defence of India Act, 1939."
Vide Statement of Objects and Reasons printed at page 194 of Part V of the
Gazette of India, 1940.]

Amendment of section 2, Act XXXV of 1939

The Defence of India (Amendment) Act, 1940
The Defence of India (Amendment) Act, 1940
Received the assent of the Governor General on the 10yh
April, 1940, and is published in the Gazette of India, Part IV, dated the 13th
April 1940.
Act No. XIX of 1940.
An Act to amend the Defence of India Act, 1939.
2. Amendment of section 2, Act
XXXV of 1939.---In section 2 of the Defence of India Act, 1939 (hereinafter
referred to as the said Act)-
(a) in clause (v) of sub-section (2),
after the words " with foreign powers " the words "or with
States in India, or to prejudice the maintenance of peaceful conditions in the
tribal areas," shall be inserted ;
(b) in
sub-section (5), after the words "not being" the brackets words
"(except in the case of a Chief Commissioner's Province)" shall
inserted.
Notes
Section 2 (a)-The clause amended
hereby enables rules to be made for the prevention of inter alia the spreading
of reports or the prosecution ca purposes likely to prejudice his Majesty's
relations with foreign powers.
The case for extending the scope
of the rule-making power in the manner proposed is clear.
Section 2 (b).--As all officers
serving in a Chief Commissioner's Pro vince are subordinate to the Central
Government, sub-section (5) of section 2, as it now stands, has the anomalous
and unintended effect of precluding a delegation by the Chief Commissioner to
any officer serving in his province.

Amendment of section 18, Act XXXV of 1939

3. Amendment of section 18,
Act XXXV of 1939.---In section 18 of the said Act, after the word
"from", in both places where it occurs, the words or in respect
of" shall be inserted.
Notes
Section 3.-The
object of this amendment is to render the benefits of the Indian Soldiers
(Litigation) Act, 1925, admissible to members of Indian States Forces while
serving in the conditions specified in the section under amendment.
